primaryListVerdict: The inherited Genius List is genuinely exhausted, but the live 241-step gate exposed five infrastructure defects behind green or advisory surfaces. The highest-value work is not another product feature: make the security scan project-scoped, stop the RUM canary from calling a 24-day telemetry blackout 'no anomaly', make missing doctor evidence non-green, unify revenue freshness across startup and doctor, and automate the task-board rotation the closeout prompt currently leaves to agent memory. Production promotion remains intentionally held.

skippedPremises.title: Add generate-build-sha --check to the blocking build gate
skippedPremises.why: Rejected on live source verification. The committed feed is intentionally generated before the closeout commit while pages-deploy stamps the exact served SHA into the deployed artifact; forcing committed HEAD equality would conflate candidate source with deployed identity and create permanent publisher churn.

skippedPremises.title: Treat zero numeric TASK_BOARD IDs as a validator failure
skippedPremises.why: Rejected after reading the validator contract. It validates duplicate IDs only in numeric table rows; the current board intentionally uses Markdown list items, so zero is an honest non-applicable count rather than a no-op over an expected table.

skippedPremises.title: Publish the stale forge journal to clear the freshness warning
skippedPremises.why: Honestly deferred. The draft is founder-voice content and the repository explicitly forbids autonomous publication; refreshing the report would be worse than preserving the warning.

skippedPremises.title: Deploy production to restore RUM telemetry and generate fresh comparison windows
skippedPremises.why: Honestly deferred. The production Worker is under an explicit auth/security promotion hold; CANON-019 does not authorize bypassing it to manufacture green telemetry.

skippedPremises.title: Use an AI summarizer for incident and release evidence
skippedPremises.why: Rejected. These are deterministic evidence contracts where an LLM would add cost and nondeterminism without improving the information-finding outcome.

skippedPremises.title: Gamify incident recovery with streaks or badges
skippedPremises.why: Rejected against SOUL and the public trust posture. Recovery evidence should be legible and accountable, not converted into a reward loop.

items.title: Scope the package-trust scan to this repository instead of all Studio checkouts
items.why: verify-supply-chain.mjs invokes the portfolio scanner without --repo, so this project's build gate walks every registered local checkout. The latest direct timing receipt shows 59.2 seconds in this one step, 34% of the complete 175.9-second gate, and violates the per-project scoping rule.
items.premise: The canonical scanner already supports --repo <slug>; the wrapper can derive the registered slug from PROJECT_STATUS and retain the same IOC depth for this repository while eliminating unrelated filesystem work.
liveEvidence: api/build-check-diagnostics.json step 86 took 59,217ms of 175,927ms total
scripts/verify-supply-chain.mjs passes only --json
studio-ops scan-npm-supply-chain.mjs filters registry targets when --repo is supplied
context/PROJECT_STATUS.json identifies vaultsparkstudios-website
items.outcome: security + speed: every local and pre-push run scans the exact project being committed, reports the scanned repo count, and removes roughly one-third of gate latency without reducing IOC coverage.
items.recipe: Resolve the canonical project slug from PROJECT_STATUS, pass --repo to the shared scanner, fail honest-dark when the slug cannot be resolved or the scanner returns malformed JSON, print scoped target evidence, and add self-tests for argument construction, malformed output, findings, and scanner failure.

L2.recipe: Derive the slug and surface scoped evidence.

L3.recipe: Extract pure helpers, add negative-path self-tests, and verify the real timing delta.

executionLog.note: Scoped the canonical IOC scanner to vaultsparkstudios-website, fixed nested-finding parsing, added 5/5 negative-path tests, and cut the real scan from 59.2s to 2.0s.

items.title: Make the RUM anomaly canary distinguish healthy, thin, stale, and empty evidence
items.why: The gate prints 'no week-over-week field anomaly detected' and '(no data rows yet)' while data/rum-history.ndjson contains 281 rows. Its newest row is 2026-07-03, so Date.now-based windows are empty during the known ingest outage; zero anomalies currently masquerades as green rather than honest-dark.
items.premise: An anomaly detector needs an evidence-state dimension separate from anomaly count. It can anchor comparison windows to the latest observation, publish ledger cardinality and age, and downgrade current coverage when the latest observation is stale without inventing an anomaly.
liveEvidence: data/rum-history.ndjson contains 281 valid rows
the newest row is dated 2026-07-03
check-rum-anomaly-canary.mjs compares only Date.now minus 7/14 days
the current artifact has routes=0, anomalies=0, ok=true
items.outcome: feedback + information-finding: maintainers can tell 'performance stable' from 'telemetry absent'; historical windows still reveal the last comparable route deltas, while the public-safe artifact reports current coverage as stale instead of green.
items.recipe: Add evidenceState and coverage metadata, anchor historical comparison to the latest complete day, retain a separate currentFreshness verdict against wall clock, make ok nullable when no current evidence exists, add empty/stale/thin/healthy/anomaly fixtures, and update console/JSON output plus build-gate expectations.

L2.recipe: Publish stale/empty/thin/healthy evidence states and nullable verdict.

L3.recipe: Anchor last-known comparison windows, preserve wall-clock freshness, add complete fixtures, and wire structural contract coverage.

executionLog.note: Canary schema v2 separates empty/thin/stale/anomaly/healthy, anchors last-known windows, reports 281 rows and 24d stale with ok=null, labels thin routes insufficient, and proves alert consumer behavior; 6/6 + 6/6 tests pass.

items.title: Stop Doctor from rendering unavailable evidence as a green check
items.why: The live Doctor prints a green check beside 'Feedback ledger score — ledger unavailable'. run-doctor.mjs explicitly returns pass:true on JSON parse failure for feedback and entropy probes, turning missing evidence into a positive health claim.
items.premise: Unavailable non-blocking evidence should be a warning with an explicit could-not-evaluate reason. Blocking failures remain separate, so honesty improves without fabricating a release blocker.
liveEvidence: node scripts/ops.mjs doctor prints Feedback ledger score with a green glyph and ledger unavailable
run-doctor.mjs feedback parse catch returns { pass: true, detail: 'ledger unavailable' }
run-doctor.mjs entropy parse catch uses the same false-green pattern
items.outcome: trust + information-finding: the health board distinguishes measured pass, measured fail, and unavailable; doctor blockingFailing remains source-derived and no absent probe can increase the score.
items.recipe: Extract a small unavailable-warning result helper, use it in feedback and entropy parse failures, add parser/self-test cases that prove unavailable never increments passing, and verify Doctor renders a warning while keeping blockingFailing 0.

L1.recipe: Change both catch branches to warning failures.

L2.recipe: Share the unavailable result and test score classification.

L3.recipe: Add self-test fixtures for malformed/missing/valid probe output and verify JSON plus board output.

executionLog.note: Unavailable feedback/entropy evidence now renders warning rather than pass; 6/6 parser tests pass and live Doctor exits 0 with 12/15, 3 warnings, blockingFailing 0.

items.title: Give startup brief and Doctor one revenue-freshness resolver
items.why: The same startup run renders 'Revenue sig. not found — stale' while Doctor reports the canonical sibling signal as six days old and fresh. The checker falls back to studio-ops; render-startup-brief.mjs reimplements the lookup against a local portfolio file that this public repo does not carry.
items.premise: A pure resolver can own candidate paths, generated-date parsing, age thresholds, and source provenance. Both surfaces can consume it and must agree for the same clock.
liveEvidence: docs/STARTUP_BRIEF.md reports revenue signal not found
node scripts/ops.mjs doctor reports revenue signals 6d old
check-revenue-freshness.mjs searches local then sibling
render-startup-brief.mjs reads only portfolio/REVENUE_SIGNALS.md locally
items.outcome: orientation + information-finding: the founder sees one current revenue-freshness verdict at startup and in Doctor, with source provenance and no contradictory red/green tiles.
items.recipe: Extract scripts/lib/revenue-freshness.mjs with pure parse/resolve/evaluate helpers, refactor checker and brief renderer to consume it, add local/sibling/missing/stale fixtures, and extend startup smoke to assert cross-surface agreement.

L1.recipe: Copy the sibling fallback into the renderer.

L2.recipe: Extract one resolver and consume it from both surfaces.

L3.recipe: Add provenance, deterministic clock injection, cross-surface fixtures, and a startup agreement contract.

executionLog.note: One pure resolver now owns local/sibling selection, thresholds, clock, and provenance; 6/6 fixtures and 58/58 startup smoke pass, and the brief now agrees with Doctor at fresh 6d.

items.title: Move TASK_BOARD rotation from remembered prose into closeout autopilot
items.why: The live size check reports 150KB and three rotatable blocks beyond the three-session window. prompts/closeout.md tells agents to run rotate-taskboard --apply, but closeout-autopilot.mjs only runs the unrelated secret rotation tripwire; repeated canonical closeouts therefore leave the board oversized.
items.premise: Closeout autopilot is the one unavoidable commit boundary and can invoke the existing idempotent project-local rotator before diff generation. A boundary contract can prevent the step from silently disappearing.
liveEvidence: rotate-taskboard --check-size reports 150KB and 3 rotatable blocks
prompts/closeout.md names rotate-taskboard --apply
closeout-autopilot.mjs Step 3c calls studio-ops rotation-tripwire.mjs, which checks secret rotation rather than TASK_BOARD
scripts/rotate-taskboard.mjs already has self-tests and an idempotent apply mode
items.outcome: navigation + speed: startup/audit agents load a bounded active board, historical rows remain preserved in archives, and every closeout enforces the size contract without relying on memory.
items.recipe: Add a project-local task-board rotation step to closeout autopilot before derived artifacts, fail closed on rotator errors, cover dry-run and real command presence in check-closeout-boundary, run the rotator now, and verify active rows plus archives retain all task evidence.

L2.recipe: Wire it into autopilot with failure handling.

L3.recipe: Add boundary tests, archive-integrity checks, dry-run visibility, and verify idempotence.

executionLog.note: Closeout autopilot now runs heading normalization plus content-preserving archive rotation before derived artifacts, fails closed, and exposes both operations in dry-run. Boundary contract self-test is 9/9; rotator self-test 23/23; live rotation moved 3 old session blocks and a second dry-run proved idempotence.

items.title: Turn the edge incident timestamp into an evidence-bounded onset interval
items.why: The public feed currently exposes only onsetNotLaterThan from the coarse uptime ledger. The committed RUM history independently proves healthy intake on 2026-07-03, but daily aggregation cannot support an invented exact timestamp; promotion history is unrelated to routed Worker semantics.
items.premise: A source-labelled interval can combine independent evidence without merging resolutions: RUM supplies a conservative last-known-healthy window/lower bound, uptime supplies a first-known-degraded upper bound, and the route ledger remains the only per-route source.
liveEvidence: data/rum-history.ndjson has its last non-empty day on 2026-07-03
data/uptime-history.ndjson transitions from up to edge-degraded at 2026-07-12T23:52:39.634Z
api/worker-route-history.json first observes route mismatch on 2026-07-26T07:10:42.158Z
data/promotion-history.ndjson records static production reconciliation only and cannot prove Worker-route state
items.outcome: information-finding + trust: humans and agents see what is known, the interval in which onset occurred, each source's resolution, and which tempting evidence was intentionally excluded; no date is presented with more precision than its ledger supports.
items.recipe: Add pure source adapters for RUM healthy windows and coarse uptime degradation, derive an onsetEvidence object with lower/upper bounds and source/resolution labels, retain onsetNotLaterThan for compatibility, render the interval on /status/, expose it through agent discovery, and test missing/conflicting/legacy evidence without hand-entering incident dates.

L1.recipe: Publish the RUM healthy day beside the existing upper bound.

L2.recipe: Derive a labelled lower/upper interval with honest unknown handling and status copy.

L3.recipe: Add reusable evidence contributions, exclusion rationale, dual-audience discovery, conflict fixtures, and UI/source contracts.

executionLog.note: Derived a source-labelled last-healthy RUM window and first-known-degraded upper bound without inventing timestamp precision.
Published contributions, interval width, exclusions, compatibility fields, status copy, agent discovery, and missing/conflict fixtures.
Verified build-worker-route-history 43/43 and status feed field contract 12/12.

items.title: Repair shell-parity truth and make the scheduled deploy receipt observe it
items.why: verify:deploy-parity exits red even against local index.html. It expects every fingerprinted asset in the global manifest on one route and its parser omits home-idle-loader, nav-sheet, sentry-init, and supabase-client, so the celebrated four-asset production drift is currently indistinguishable from a detector bug.
items.premise: The correct contract is route-local source HTML versus the same deployed route, using one generic fingerprint parser. The existing uptime publisher already owns deploy-currency observation, so extending that receipt avoids another workflow and keeps SHA currency plus shell parity in one truth surface.
liveEvidence: npm run verify:deploy-parity exits 1 with source=index.html and four missing assets
index.html actually references home-idle-loader, nav-sheet, and sentry-init
check-deploy-parity.mjs regex cannot parse those asset names and compares against all manifest assets
check-staging-parity.mjs independently duplicates a similarly incomplete shell parser
.github/workflows/uptime-probe.yml already runs build-deploy-currency.mjs --probe every 30 minutes
items.outcome: release confidence + information-finding: the command is green on byte-current local source, red only on real route-local production drift, and the scheduled public receipt reports exact missing/unexpected shells alongside SHA age for humans and agents.
items.recipe: Extract one generic shell-path parser/comparator, make deploy parity compare local route HTML to deployed route HTML, add unreachable/challenge/route fixtures, fold the bounded result into deploy-currency without overwriting the last usable observation, advertise the receipt to agents/status proof, and wire focused self-tests into build:check.

L1.recipe: Fix the regex and local false-positive.

L2.recipe: Compare route-local source and deployed HTML with pure fixtures.

L3.recipe: Share the parser with staging, extend scheduled deploy-currency truth, integrate discovery/proof surfaces, and cover challenge/retention semantics.

executionLog.note: Replaced the incomplete global-manifest regex with one generic route-local parser shared by production and staging.
Made verify:deploy-parity a real production probe and folded challenge-resistant shell observations into deploy-currency, release proof, status proof, evidence graph, and agent discovery.
Added a second-order structural contract that rejects --local production callers and parser duplication; focused suites pass 26/26 + 7/7 + 4/4.

items.title: Make the first real Worker recovery close itself exactly once and prove every consequence
items.why: The semantic ledger's synthetic test closes one route, but production has never produced a matched transition. The eventual recovery must append one semantic row, close every open incident at the same observation, freeze durations, and drive /status/ to its healthy branch without relying on a human to notice.
items.premise: The scheduled publisher is the correct enforcement point. It sees the previous ledger, the fresh receipt, and the derived feed in one process, so it can validate a real mismatch-to-matched transition without inventing recovery data now.
liveEvidence: data/worker-route-history.ndjson contains only one mismatch genesis row
build-worker-route-history.mjs appendIfChanged and buildIncidents already expose the transition inputs
status/index.html already has open and no-open branches but no source-level contract binds them to the feed
Production remains 0/5 matched, so any claim that real recovery passed today would be fabricated
items.outcome: feedback loop + security: when reality flips, the publisher either emits one internally coherent closure or fails loudly; until then the feed says awaiting-real-recovery and the audit records live proof as honestly deferred.
items.recipe: Add a pure recovery-transition validator and recovery object to the existing feed, enforce close-once/all-open-routes-closed/duration-frozen invariants during the real append path, add replay and recurrence fixtures, and add a status source contract for the healthy branch. Keep the TASK_BOARD proof item open until a real matched row exists.

L2.recipe: Validate real append transitions and publish awaiting/closed state.

L3.recipe: Prove close-once, all-route closure, frozen duration, recurrence, status branch, and preserve an explicit live-proof deferral.

executionLog.note: Enforced close-once, exact-open-set closure, all-routes-matched, duplicate-observation rejection, frozen duration, and verified-prior-recovery recurrence semantics.
Published a stable awaiting-real-recovery schema and bound the healthy status branch to liveProofAvailable.
Real recovery proof remains intentionally open because production is still mismatch and the auth/security promotion interlock is founder-held; no recovery row was fabricated.
